Chapter 10. Living the Absurd: Everyday Life and the Ongoing Struggle.
Picture yourself waking up to yet another ordinary day. Maybe you feel the weight of that familiar routine... the sense that nothing ever really changes. But here's the thing—just getting up, facing whatever the day throws at you, and doing what needs to be done... that’s a quiet kind of heroism.
The struggle doesn’t continue because there’s some promise of victory. It’s because living, in itself, is an act of rebellion.
Most of us don’t even notice the absurdity woven into our daily lives. We’re busy—caught up in work, family, streaming another show. But every once in a while, that question sneaks up: Why am I doing any of this?
And if there’s an answer, it’s not found in big grand gestures. It’s tucked away in the small things—the little acts of courage and kindness that fill up our days.
Think about a friend who reaches out when you’re having a tough time. Or a stranger who offers a genuine smile. Maybe it’s just taking pride in a job well done, even if nobody notices. These are the moments that spark meaning in our lives, even when the world itself stays silent.
The absurd is always lurking in the background, but so is the chance for joy, for real connection, for creating something new—even if it’s just a fleeting moment.
Living the absurd isn’t about giving up hope. It’s about letting go of the need for certainty. It’s accepting the world as it is, and choosing to live fully—right here, right now.
There’s a unique kind of freedom in facing the struggle head-on, and in finding meaning simply by being alive and present.
